setup: Forearms on a bench or your thighs
Palms down, wrists just past the edge
execution: Let your hands drop toward the floor
Lift the backs of your hands up
Raise as high as your wrists allow
faults: Don't lift your elbows to help

notes: This side of the forearm is much weaker than the palm side: start very light.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Dumbbell wrist extension
regressions.reason: One light dumbbell per hand; each wrist works alone.

progressions.name: Reverse wrist curl with a pause
progressions.reason: A hold at the top adds difficulty without more weight.

substitutions.name: Dumbbell wrist extension
substitutions.reason: Same movement; load is each dumbbell.

substitutions.name: Reverse curl
substitutions.reason: Overhand curl; the wrist extensors hold the wrist straight.

substitutions.name: Wrist roller
substitutions.reason: Rolling the weight up works both sides of the forearm.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Close side view at bench height, forearms along a flat bench with the hands just past the edge on the right, palms down. Hands and forearms fill most of the frame.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Forearms flat along the bench, palms down, wrists over the edge. Hands dropped so the bar hangs below the bench top.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Backs of the hands lifted so the knuckles point up, bar raised above the bench top. Forearms still flat.

guideBrief.barPath: A short arc around the wrists
